newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes weaken late, eye support from gasoline.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes weaken late, eye support from gasoline.

text.p: U.S. crudes weakened Tuesday into the expiry of NYMEX November crude and ample near-term supplies, but eyed gasoline's uptrend for support.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) report showed a build of 5.6 million barrels in crude oil stocks, aggravated by a tide of 8.1 million barrels per day of imports.
But this was partly offset by more bullish gasoline data, showing a draw of nearly 6.0 million barrels.
December West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $25.45-55 a barrel, up 10 cents from Monday. November levels were easier due to the flattening of the Nov/Dec backwardation.
The Nov/Dec WTI spread pulled back to 27-30 cents, off from the morning's level of nearly 40 cents.
Traders predicted a more bearish tone, due to the latest API statistics and looked to domestic grades easing shortly into the deadline for Nov pipeline nominations on Friday.

Sweet and sour grades continued to diverge as traders paid up for Louisiana crudes in the early session, but sold off West Texas Sour ahead of the government's Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) sale, and surpluses from Latin America.
Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) shutting down a 108,000 bpd catcracker at its Amuay refinery added pressure on sours.
West Texas Sour/Midland traded from WTI minus $1.51 to $1.60, with bids retreating beyond the last trade.
Traders said an influx of Canadian and Californian crude also added to excess sours in the near-term.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire kept steady at a premium of 75-80 cents a barrel, but no trades were seen.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St James traded first at WTI plus 71 cents before receding to 67 cents.
The tight Brent/West Texas Intermediate arbitrage, which has drained distillate-rich North Sea and West African imports from the Gulf Coast, continued to lend support.
